territorial_scope.description: Applies to persons conducting business in Tennessee that produce products or services targeting Tennessee residents and meet the revenue and consumer-count tests.

evidence.quote: This part applies to persons that conduct business in this state producing products or services that target residents of this state

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Tennessee's consumer data privacy statute gives state residents access, correction, deletion, portability and opt-out rights and imposes controller and processor duties on large businesses meeting revenue and consumer-count thresholds; the attorney general enforces it. Effective 1 July 2025.
summary.long: Adds a Tennessee consumer personal-information part (Title 47, Ch. 18). Covers businesses producing products or services targeting Tennessee residents that exceed $25 million in revenue and meet a consumer-count or data-sale test; excludes state bodies, financial institutions, HIPAA-covered entities, nonprofits and higher-education institutions. Consumers gain access, correction, deletion, portability and opt-out rights (sale, targeted advertising, certain profiling); controllers must respond within 45 days, limit collection, secure data, obtain consent for sensitive data, publish privacy notices and conduct data protection assessments for targeted advertising, sales, certain profiling and sensitive data. Processors act under binding contracts. The attorney general enforces exclusively after a 60-day cure notice, with civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation and treble damages for willful or knowing violations; no private right of action. A NIST-conforming privacy program is an affirmative defense. Preempts conflicting local ordinances; effective July 1, 2025.

notes: The long title lists ten Titles of the Tennessee Code, but the only operative amendment (Section 2) adds a part to Title 47, Chapter 18. Section 47-18-3204(a)(5) refers to 47-18-3203(a)(2)(F), but 47-18-3203(a)(2) ends at subdivision (E). Section 47-18-3206(f) applies data protection assessment requirements to processing from July 1, 2024, while Section 6 sets the act's effective date as July 1, 2025. The scanned text has OCR artifacts: many subdivision letters (B) appear as (8), and some quotes contain such characters. The text is the 2023 enacted version; no consolidated code text was checked.
